label: Entity resolution and link clustering
summary: A runnable reference for deciding which records belong to the same real-world group from shared attributes: candidate blocking, rarity-weighted pair features, a pair classifier, clustering by connected components and a check on the largest cluster.
runtime: Python 3.11+ with numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy and pytest (about 3 seconds)
run: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
expected: make_data.py prints about 3,200 entities in 1,800 true clusters. baseline.py reports on held-out clusters: linking everything that shares any value gives one cluster of 342 entities and pair precision 0.02 at recall 0.80; the rarity-weighted pair model gives pair precision 0.98 at recall 0.79, purity 0.996 and a largest cluster of 9. pytest reports 7 passed.

files.purpose: Synthetic entities with shared and noisy attributes, hub values that link unrelated entities and hidden true clusters
Blocking, rarity-weighted pair features, pair classifier, union-find clustering and pairwise and cluster metrics
Executable gates: determinism, hubs, blocking, transitivity, metric arithmetic and the two clusterings

synthetic.description: About 3,200 entities in 1,800 clusters (most singletons) with phone, device, address, name and network address; 8% of values missing, 30% of names with a typo, and a dozen hub network addresses shared by dozens of unrelated entities.
knobs: hub_share and n_hubs: how many entities sit behind a hub value
seed: identical seed gives an identical graph

slots.meaning: how many entities share each linking value, so a value shared by three says more than one shared by three hundred
how many different kinds of value two records share
character-level overlap of the two names, tolerant of typos

slots.feature: group size of the rarest shared value
slots.meaning: log of the size of the smallest group the pair shares
whether a shared value is a known hub

data.threshold: pytest -k 'deterministic or hub' passes: more than 50% of entities are singletons, one hub value links more than 20 entities and train and test share 0 clusters
data.how: Run pytest in the kit directory

features.threshold: Blocking skips missing values (-1) and proposes only the 1 pair that shares a real value; links A-B and B-C put A and C in 1 cluster

baseline.threshold: Linking on any shared value gives pair precision below 0.2 and a largest cluster of at least 100 (the kit: 0.02 and 342)

challenger.metric: Pair precision and recall with cluster size
challenger.threshold: Pair precision at least 0.9, recall at least 0.7, purity at least 0.95 and a largest cluster of at most 30 (the kit: 0.98, 0.79, 0.996 and 9)

tests.pass: One value links more than 20 entities that mostly belong to different real groups
Only the pair that shares a real value is proposed
A-B and B-C links put A and C in one cluster
Pair precision 1/3, recall 1/2 and largest cluster 3 on the toy example
Linking on any shared value gives precision below 0.2 and a cluster of at least 100
Pair precision at least 0.9 and recall at least 0.7 with a largest cluster of at most 30

lessons.trap: Linking everything that shares any value
lessons.evidence: One hub address joins hundreds of strangers: the largest cluster has 342 entities and pair precision is 0.02.

lessons.trap: Ignoring how rare a shared value is
lessons.evidence: Weighting each shared value by the inverse log of its group size lifts pair precision to 0.98 at the same recall.

lessons.trap: Evaluating on clusters the model has seen
lessons.evidence: The kit holds out whole clusters, not pairs, so no true group appears in both train and test.
A single wrong link between two real groups merges them completely, so the largest cluster is monitored.

target: A pair of records is positive when both belong to the same hidden true cluster. Clusters are formed by connected components over the pairs the model links.
